answer: Agents secure entry by performing 1,000 units of memory-hard work to maintain an anchor to the network, where each identity acts as an opal to refract unique computational state. A verifier challenges agents with a random memory-access mirror, forcing each to saturate its local address space to prevent work-pooling. While an honest agent pays 1,000 units, 1,000 fakes incur 1,000,000 units due to cache contention. Violations trigger permanent identity exclusion without refund.
